hints: Focus on what it means that solid CO2 is similar to solid iodine in structure and properties.
Remember iodine forms a molecular crystal, while silica is famous for being a very hard, very high melting point giant solid.
Think about which word describes both a molecular crystal and a giant covalent network, and check bonding and sublimation for CO2 versus SiO2.
walkthrough:
**Identify the structure of solid CO2**

Think of dry ice. The question tells you it is like solid iodine.

Iodine is $\text{I}_2$ molecules held together by weak van der Waals forces in a regular arrangement. Solid $\text{CO}_2$ is the same, discrete $\text{O=C=O}$ molecules in a molecular lattice.

**Identify the structure of solid SiO2**

Silica does not exist as separate $\text{SiO}_2$ molecules. Each Si is tetrahedrally bonded to four O atoms, and each O bridges two Si atoms.

This gives a giant covalent (macromolecular) lattice with very strong bonds throughout, like diamond.

**Compare and choose the common statement**

Both types of arrangement are called lattices, just different kinds: molecular lattice for $\text{CO}_2$ and giant covalent lattice for $\text{SiO}_2$.

So the only statement true for both is that both exist in a lattice structure.

options.A: Correct. Both are ordered 3D arrangements, so both are lattices. Solid CO2 has a simple molecular lattice and solid SiO2 has a giant covalent lattice.
options.B: Only solid CO2 is simple molecular. SiO2 is giant covalent with no discrete SiO2 molecules, so this is false. The trap is assuming Group 14 oxides must have the same structure.
options.C: Only SiO2 has all single bonds ($\text{Si-O}$). CO2 has double bonds ($\text{O=C=O}$). The trap is thinking both Group 14 dioxides bond in the same way.
options.D: Only solid CO2 sublimes spontaneously at s.t.p. (dry ice). SiO2 has a very high melting point above 1600 C due to strong giant covalent bonds, so this is false.
